name: Desmoplastic/Nodular Medulloblastoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System (2021)

criteria.description: Presence of nodular/desmoplastic histological pattern with reticulin-rich internodular zones
Positive staining for synaptophysin and neuronal markers with absence of classic medulloblastoma features
WNT or SHH molecular subgroup confirmation, commonly SHH-activated
MRI showing cerebellar mass with nodular enhancement and desmoplastic features

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of nodular/desmoplastic pattern plus molecular subgrouping consistent with SHH activation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular subgrouping is critical for prognosis and treatment planning.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Posterior fossa tumor causing increased intracranial pressure
searchTerms: tumor in back of brain causing pressure
posterior fossa mass increasing brain pressure

common.symptomName: Headache due to raised intracranial pressure
searchTerms: headache due to raised intracranial pressure

common.symptomName: Nausea and vomiting secondary to increased intracranial pressure
searchTerms: nausea caused by increased brain pressure

common.symptomName: Ataxia and gait disturbance from cerebellar involvement
Hydrocephalus due to obstruction of cerebrospinal fluid pathways
searchTerms: water on the brain from blockage
cranial nerve palsies causing facial or eye problems
unusual changes in behavior or mood

rare.symptomName: Endocrine dysfunction due to hypothalamic involvement
searchTerms: hormone problems from brain area damage
endocrine issues due to hypothalamus involvement
hormonal imbalance caused by brain tumor
tingling or pins and needles in face

laboratory: CSF cytology may show malignant cells
Elevated intracranial pressure on lumbar puncture opening pressure
imaging: MRI showing posterior fossa mass with nodular and desmoplastic features
other: Histopathology demonstrating nodular/desmoplastic architecture with reticulin staining

distinguishingFeatures: Generally cystic with mural nodule on imaging

redFlags: Signs of increased intracranial pressure such as papilledema
New onset seizures in a child with posterior fossa mass
references: Louis DN, et al. WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System, 5th Edition, 2021.
Taylor MD, et al. Molecular subgroups of medulloblastoma: the current consensus. Acta Neuropathol. 2012.
